ops.title: Namespace hooks import can be shadowed by stale regular hooks package in tests
ops.body:
# Hook source identity test order failure

The original `tests/test_pack_imports.py::test_primitive_source_identity_matches_project_hook_for_both_hosts` passed alone and with its own module, but failed after `tests/test_faults.py::test_discover_registers_the_fault_announcer`. In a frozen test copy, that exact two-test sequence produced an empty hook set and `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hooks.guard'` in `captain_hook.loader.discover_hooks`.

`test_discover_registers_the_fault_announcer` creates a regular `.claude/hooks` package with `__init__.py`, then `CliState.discover()` adds its parent to `sys.path`. The test has no `isolate_modules` fixture, so the path remains. The original source identity test deletes `hooks` entries from `sys.modules`, then discovers a new `.capt-hook/hooks` directory without `__init__.py`. Python's import finder selects the earlier regular `hooks` package from the stale path instead of the new namespace package, and `hooks.guard` cannot load. The loader records the error and continues, leaving the observed hooks empty.

The current test-only correction runs each host's discovery in a fresh subprocess with the test project's root as cwd and the package root on PYTHONPATH, then retains the same assertions on host parity and each hook’s identity and source. This isolates inherited `sys.path` and `sys.modules` without weakening expectations. A narrower producer cleanup would be to add `isolate_modules` to the `test_discover_registers_the_fault_announcer` fixture list, but the subprocess correction directly protects the two-host test from any earlier package-path pollution.

Verification ran in `/tmp/codex-port-hook-order-verify`. The original target failed after the single producer with an empty identity set and `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hooks.guard'`; the output is in `/tmp/codex-port-hook-order-baseline.log`. The current target passed that two-test sequence. Both complete test modules passed together, with 25 tests passing.

This diagnosis changed no shared source, wheel, global installation, or release artifact. A full make was not run.
